Test Description: Validate default reset values and read/write behavior of GPIO_8 to GPIO_27 registers over the AHB register interface using predefined read/write masks and multiple data patterns. Non-readable or non-writable registers are skipped per masks; expected readback accounts for preserved default bits where writes are masked off.
Meta Test Description: The test verifies default values and R/W functionality for a set of GPIO registers listed in addr_array (GPIO_8..GPIO_27). It first runs chk_rst_val(): for each address i in [0..CNT-1], it skips if skip_rst_array[i]==1; if read_mask_array[i]==0x00000000, it skips as not readable. Otherwise it performs data_rd = read_reg(addr_array[i]) and masks with 0xfffffffe to ignore bit0, then compares against default_value_array[i]; on mismatch increments def_fail_cnt and logs failure. Next, chk_rd_wr(): defines six patterns {0xffffffff, 0xaaaaaaaa, 0x55555555, 0xf5f5f5f5, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xffff0000}. For each pattern, it writes (data_wr & write_mask_array[i]) to each address i that is not skipped (skip_array[i]==0) and is writable (write_mask_array[i]!=0). It then reads back for each address i that is not skipped, writable, and readable (read_mask_array[i]!=0) using data_rd = read_reg(addr) & read_mask_array[i]. Expected exp_val is computed as: (data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | ((~write_mask_array[i]) & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i]). It compares data_rd with exp_val; on mismatch increments wr_fail_cnt and logs. At the end of test_case(), if def_fail_cnt>0 or wr_fail_cnt>0 calls finish(1) else finish(0). A soft_reset_chk() routine exists but is compiled out (#ifdef 0).
Remarks: Default value check intentionally masks bit0 to avoid false mismatches due to input sampling behavior. Registers with read mask of 0 are treated as non-readable and skipped; registers with write mask of 0 are treated as non-writable and skipped. Expected readback preserves default bits where writes are masked off. Ensure that the iteration count matches the size of the control arrays to avoid out-of-bounds access. When inputs are not forced, some input bits may read high; forcing zero can affect level selection and lead to mismatches, hence the mask of bit0 in default check.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Initialize the GPIO register list (GPIO_8 through GPIO_27) with associated default, read-mask, and write-mask data.
2) Default value verification: For each GPIO register that is readable and not marked to skip, read the register and compare its value (with bit0 ignored) against the documented default value. Record any mismatches.
3) Write/read verification: For each of the six data patterns, write the pattern masked by each register’s write mask to all writable, non-skipped GPIO registers; then read back the value masked by each register’s read mask and compare against the expected value computed from the written bits plus preserved default bits where writes are masked. Record any mismatches.
4) Determine pass/fail: If no default or write/read mismatches were recorded, declare PASS; otherwise, declare FAIL.
Impacted Registers: GPIO_8, GPIO_9, GPIO_10, GPIO_11, GPIO_12, GPIO_13, GPIO_14, GPIO_15, GPIO_16, GPIO_17, GPIO_18, GPIO_19, GPIO_20, GPIO_21, GPIO_22, GPIO_23, GPIO_24, GPIO_25, GPIO_26, GPIO_27
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: PASS if, for all GPIO_8–GPIO_27: (a) the default read value (with bit0 ignored) matches the documented default when readable; and (b) for each test pattern, the masked readback equals (written-bits & write-mask & read-mask) OR (preserved-default-bits & ~write-mask & read-mask). Any mismatch results in FAIL.

Test Description: Verify that enabling negative-edge interrupts per GPIO pad (GPIO_8–GPIO_39) correctly generates an interrupt on a falling edge, sets the group status bit, and can be cleared via per-pin raw-clear and system raw status clear, with proper ISR handling.
Meta Test Description: In test_case(): Optionally enable GIC IRQ 87/88. Enable system-level GPIO interrupt output via INTREN1 for GPIO0/GPIO1. Drive pad output register at 0xA0243ffc high. For i in 0..31: configure each per-pin control at (GPIO_8 + i*4) with bits (1<<20)|(1<<18)|(1<<16) (configures negedge enable and clears raw). For each i: wr_val=1<<i; clear group raw status by writing wr_val to RAWSTCR1; enable group interrupt output for bit i by writing wr_val to GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1; set int_pend=1; drive 0xA0243ffc high then ~wr_val to create a falling edge on the selected pad; poll with timeout until int_pend is cleared by ISR; on timeout, record error. Call finish(test_err). Default_IRQHandler(): compute local_wr=1<<i; set int_pend=0; drive 0xA0243ffc high; read per-pin register raddr=(GPIO_8 + i*4) to rdata; if (rdata & 0x1)!=0 then error; if ((rdata & 0x2)!=0x0) then read group status GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1; if ((rdata_grp & local_wr)==0) error; write per-pin register with (1<<20)|(1<<16) to clear; write local_wr to RAWSTCR1 to clear raw; read GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 and require 0; clear system RAWSTCR1 for GPIO0/GPIO1 and GIC clear; else branch increments error.
Remarks: Requires system interrupt enable and GIC configuration. Test toggles an external pad drive at 0xA0243ffc to generate edges; ensure this mapping drives GPIO_8–GPIO_39 lines as expected. Group raw status must be cleared in both GPIO block and system controller after service.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: PASS if each GPIO pad from GPIO_8 to GPIO_39 generates a negative-edge interrupt when driven from high to low, the corresponding group interrupt status bit sets, and both per-pin and group/system raw status are successfully cleared in the ISR, with no timeouts.

Test Description: Verify that enabling positive-edge interrupts across GPIO_8–GPIO_39 generates an interrupt on a rising edge for each pad, that group interrupt status is asserted, and that per-pin raw status and system raw status can be cleared; ensure GIC/system and GPIO block interactions function correctly.
Meta Test Description: test_case(): Optionally enable GIC IRQ 87/88. Enable system-level GPIO interrupt via INTREN1 for GPIO0/1. For i in 0..31, write per-pin control at (GPIO_8 + i*4) with 0x00020000 (enable posedge). Set GPIO IO mode to input via IO control group registers (GROUP1..GROUP4 set to 0x000000FF). Enable group interrupt outputs by writing 0xFFFFFFFF to GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1. For each i: drive pad output low (0xA0243ffc=0x00000000), wait, set int_pend=1, then drive high (0xA0243ffc=0xFFFFFFFF) to create a rising edge; wait with timeout until ISR clears int_pend; drive low again to prepare for next iteration. Default_IRQHandler(): wr_val=1<<i; int_pend=0; read GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1; mask group interrupt during service (write 0 to GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1). If group status non-zero, proceed; else flag error. Clear per-pin raw status for all 32 pins by writing 0x00010000 to each (GPIO_8 + j*4) and wait. Read GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 and require it to be 0. Clear system RAWSTCR1 for GPIO0/1 and read back to ensure cleared. Re-enable GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, then clear GIC IRQ.
Remarks: Requires system interrupt configuration and GIC enable. GPIO group IO control must set pads to input mode before edge generation. The external pad drive at 0xA0243ffc must map to GPIO_8–GPIO_39 lines to produce edges reliably.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: PASS if, for each GPIO_8–GPIO_39 pad, a rising edge generates an interrupt that asserts the group status, and the per-pin raw status and group/system status are successfully cleared in the ISR, with no timeouts.
